correctness.rationale: On the dense invariant exponential-polynomial domain, pluriharmonic Toeplitz operators become finite Weyl differential-difference operators. Their normal forms embed faithfully in twisted crossed products of the Weyl algebra by finitely generated torsion-free abelian frequency groups; ordered leading support and the Weyl-domain property rule out zero divisors. Gaussian averaging gives symbol injectivity, and exponential-vector Taylor expansion gives a polynomial witness.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Qin's current v1 asks the one-sided zero-product question for pluriharmonic exponential-type symbols. Bauer--Choe--Koo address commuting/semicommuting structure, Cichoń develops exponential-polynomial adjoint calculus, and Cho--Park--Zhu study bounded holomorphic/antiholomorphic products. Targeted exact and synonymous searches found no finite-frequency pluriharmonic zero-divisor-free theorem, all-dimension finite-product extension, or polynomial-test strengthening.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a structurally natural positive island inside a newly sharpened open boundary: finite exponential frequency forces Toeplitz quantization into a zero-divisor-free crossed-product algebra. It also shows that any counterexample to the full pluriharmonic exponential-type question must leave the finite-frequency exponential-polynomial regime.
